financial_summary: HEMNET GROUP AB is a small-cap communication services business with a $447M market cap on $149M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 27% against a 8% cost of capital — a 19-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 101% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $56M in free cash flow — roughly 37 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.15× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 36× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 15.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
